title: Introduce KMS Introspector, Residency Soft-Guard, and Audit Obfuscator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a KMS metadata introspector service, a residency soft-guard policy shim that can fallback to compatible key pools when strict residency enforcement is not configured, and an audit obfuscator that pseudonymizes operator/service principal identities while preserving traceability for security analysts.
description:
Motivation: We saw two incidents where KMS selection mismatches caused requests to be routed to non-preferred regions, and audit logs exposed full service-principal identifiers in downstream systems. This PR adds three coordinated changes: 1) a lightweight KMS Introspector to fetch and cache key metadata (region, provider, tags) for decisioning; 2) Residency Soft-Guard, a policy shim that enforces residency decisions but allows configured soft fallbacks with enriched audit annotations; 3) Audit Obfuscator, an opt-in audit layer that pseudonymizes operator/service principal IDs using a per-tenant salt stored in the secrets store.

Summary of changes (single continuous narrative): The Introspector exposes an internal read-only API (kms_introspector.v1) used by the runtime routing layer and by the policy-enforcer to determine key residency claims without performing decrypt/encrypt operations. Residency Soft-Guard plugs into the RBAC v2 policy evaluation pipeline: when a request would violate a strict residency rule, Soft-Guard will consult fallback profiles (configured per-tenant) and, if a compatible fallback exists, allow the request with an audit annotation explaining the substitution. If no fallback exists and the tenant is in strict mode, the request is rejected. Audit Obfuscator runs as a final step before log export: it replaces full subject identifiers with salted pseudonyms and emits a keyed mapping to the internal audit vault accessible only to security ops. The mapping is HMAC-SHA256(salt, subject) with tenant salt rotation support.

- Aisha Patel (author): "Updated cache to be tenant-configurable and plumbed a fail-closed behavior for the mapping vault. Implementation note: when vault is unavailable and tenant is strict, we reject export; when soft mode, we emit 'subject=unmapped-placeholder' plus alert to ops."

notes_for_ops: Feature flags: helm.values.features.kmsIntrospector (bool), features.residencySoftGuard.mode (strict|soft). Default: disabled in stable; enabled in canary. Operators must provision per-tenant salt in secrets/vault/tenant-salts/<tenant-id>. Rolling rotation requires replay window setting to avoid mapping mismatches.
testing_instructions: Stage: deploy with helm values enabling kmsIntrospector and residencySoftGuard.mode=soft. Run tests/integration/residency_softguard_test.go against mocked KMS endpoints. Validate audit exporter emits pseudonyms and that mapping vault entries are created. For strict tenants, assert requests are rejected when no compatible key found.
known_limitations: Introspector relies on KMS metadata tags; legacy keys without region tags will be treated as 'unknown' and require operator remediation. Audit mapping vault is an internal scoped secret — if that service is unavailable, exports behave as configured per-tenant (fail-closed for strict, placeholder for soft).
follow_up: Planned follow-ups: (1) UI in Console to visualize fallback decisions and mapping lookup traces (ENG-2380); (2) add automated migration tool to backfill missing key-region tags (SEC-130); (3) evaluate adding cryptographic blinding to pseudonyms to support cross-tenant correlation under consented forensics flow.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing existing RBAC decision semantics in strict mode; Soft-Guard is opt-in per-tenant. Audit Obfuscator is opt-in per-export-target. All changes behind feature flags until staged canary validates traffic patterns.
